source: Synthetic, against the public sample app. A clean feature: every criterion has a test whose assertion would fail without it, and the Changelog's reason still holds (the print view sorts through the same sorted()). Bait: nothing to fix. Measures false alarms. To be case-reviewed before any precision run. Added 13 Nov for step 6, before any variant ran on it.
task: Review this finished feature as the feature reviewer. The Shape, the Changelog, and every merged slice's tests and code are below.
output: Reply with the JSON array of findings: [{ "id": "<short-id>", "severity": "blocking|major|minor", "text": "…", "where": "<file:line or slice>" }] (or [] when there is nothing to fix), then a line "VERDICTS:" and a JSON array with one entry per criterion: [{ "criterion": "AC-1", "verdict": "met|unmet|deferred", "tests": ["<file>: <test name>"], "slices": [1] }].
notes: Case review (13 Nov, before any precision run; contract feature reviewer, Codex and Claude, k=2): all four runs found that AC-1's unit test ('ubik', 'Dune', 'emma') gives the same order under a case-sensitive sort, so the 'ignoring case' part was unasserted; two runs noted the print view traced to no criterion. Fixed: the test now uses 'Ubik', 'dune', 'Emma' (a case-sensitive sort gives a different order), and AC-4 covers the print view. Review runs are kept out of the results. Re-review after the fix (13 Nov, k=1 per engine): every criterion met on both; only minor findings (the sorted-or-added choice is written in two places; suspected: no test that printing passes the toggle state). Accepted as minor: neither changes a verdict, and minor findings don't count against this case's precision check.
